old: A 1945 10 centavos from Mexico. Value side big 10, CENTAVOS, 1945, national arms reverse. Struck in bronze.
new: A 1945 10 centavos from Mexico. Value side big 10, CENTAVOS, 1945, national arms reverse. Struck in copper-nickel (80% copper, 20% nickel).
source: Numista N#6694 (https://en.numista.com/catalogue/pieces6694.html): Mexico 10 centavos 1936-1946 is KM# 432, composition copper-nickel (80% Cu, 20% Ni), 1945 row 9 558 000. The story said 'Struck in bronze', copied from the type record (MX.KM.433 composition 'bronze'); the record's KM 433 and bronze are corrected in the pending Numista sweep file changes_grok-bot_20261008-0035.jsonl (not merged yet), so the story follows the Numista entry. Only the metal was changed.

old: A 2006 1 baht from Thailand. The obverse shows Rama IX (Bhumibol Adulyadej) left-facing with glasses; the reverse shows Wat Phra Kaew; ประเทศไทย, พ.ศ. ๒๕๔๙, ๑ บาท. Struck in CuNi (nickel-clad steel common for type).
new: A 2006 1 baht from Thailand. The obverse shows Rama IX (Bhumibol Adulyadej) left-facing with glasses; the reverse shows Wat Phra Kaew; ประเทศไทย, พ.ศ. ๒๕๔๙, ๑ บาท. Struck in copper-nickel.
source: Numista N#1106 (https://en.numista.com/catalogue/pieces1106.html): 1 baht Rama IX non-magnetic 1986-2008 (Y# 183), composition copper-nickel. The story ended 'Struck in CuNi (nickel-clad steel common for type)'; nickel-clad steel is a different, magnetic type, not this one. The record's composition text is corrected to 'copper-nickel' in the pending sweep file changes_grok-bot_20261008-0035.jsonl. Only the metal sentence was changed.

old: A 1973 1 krona from Sweden. The obverse shows Gustaf VI Adolf left; the reverse shows crowned arms; GUSTAF VI ADOLF SVERIGES KONUNG, 1 KRONA, date. Struck in CuNi.
new: A 1973 1 krona from Sweden. The obverse shows King Gustaf VI Adolf facing left, with the words GUSTAF VI ADOLF SVERIGES KONUNG (Gustaf VI Adolf, King of Sweden); the reverse shows the crowned Swedish arms with the date, 1 KR and the motto PLIKTEN FRAMFÖR ALLT (Duty above all). Struck in copper-nickel.
source: Numista N#1516 (https://en.numista.com/catalogue/pieces1516.html): reverse lettering '1972 1 KR PLIKTEN • FRAMFÖR • ALLT' (crowned arms dividing the date, value in the middle); obverse lettering 'GUSTAF VI ADOLF SVERIGES KONUNG'; composition copper-nickel clad copper-nickel. The story said the coin reads '1 KRONA'; the coin reads 1 KR, with the motto. Shorthand 'CuNi' written out.

old: A 2015 5 pence from United Kingdom. The obverse shows Ian Rank-Broadley Elizabeth II; the reverse shows Royal Shield segment; FIVE PENCE (Matthew Dent). Struck in nickel-plated steel.
new: A 2015 5 pence from United Kingdom. The obverse shows Jody Clark's portrait of Elizabeth II; the reverse shows Royal Shield segment; FIVE PENCE (Matthew Dent). Struck in nickel-plated steel.
source: Record: C183 type GB.KM.1334 (5th portrait, Numista N#70547 https://en.numista.com/catalogue/pieces70547.html: KM# 1334, 2015 row 536 600 000) and C183 issue.mintage 536 600 000 = the Jody Clark figure in C183 mintage_text; photo C183_obv.webp shows the Clark crowned portrait with the legend ELIZABETH II DEI GRA REG FID DEF 2015 (the Rank-Broadley portrait reads D·G·REG·F·D). The story said the obverse is Ian Rank-Broadley's portrait, which contradicts the record. Only the portrait name was changed.
